title: Life-of-Tread Cancellation Refund Worksheet — Road Hazard Protection
content:
**Refund on a holder's cancellation of a Crestline Road Hazard Life-of-Tread Protection certificate bought in cash, by debit card or on a bank credit card, where no void-before-install, covered-set-returned or full-refund-window refund applies.**

| Line | Quantity | How it is figured |
|---|---|---|
| A | Certificate price | the price per tire multiplied by the number of tires covered, as recorded on the certificate |
| B | Counting date | the cancellation date |
| C | Unused share | the whole calendar months remaining from the counting date to the expiration date (a partial month not counted), divided by the plan term in months (the Life-of-Tread term on the plan's term schedule) |
| D | Prorated amount | line A multiplied by line C, rounded half up to the cent |
| E | Cancellation fee | the plan's administration fee on the Road Hazard Protection cancellation schedule |
| F | Benefits paid | the total of the amounts of the certificate's replacement entries, out-of-area reimbursement entries and roadside service entries |
| G | Refund | line D less line E less line F; after every addition to it and deduction from it that applies, it is rounded half up to the cent and held at 0.00 or more |

The refund is paid to the tender the certificate was bought with.

**Worked example (hypothetical certificate).** Four tires at 30.00 give a certificate price of 120.00. With 30 whole months remaining from the counting date in a 72-month term, the unused share is 30 divided by 72, and the prorated amount is 120.00 multiplied by 30 and divided by 72, which is 50.00. With a hypothetical fee of 25.00 and benefits paid of 18.40, the refund is 50.00 less 25.00 less 18.40, which is 6.60. Had the benefits paid been 40.00, the refund would be held at 0.00.

**Counting the months.** Whole months are counted to the same day of the month: from a hypothetical counting date of March 20 to an expiration date of September 15 of the same year there are 5 whole months (to August 20), the remaining days not counted.
